Get deeper into the guitar — and into the music.

Jazz Guitar Foundations is for intermediate players who want to expand their craft on the instrument. Across six sessions, you'll work on the physical, mental, and creative sides of jazz guitar — rhythm, tone, technique, fretboard fluency, harmony, comping, melody, improvisation, listening, and composition — in a small group, at a pace that meets you where you are.

Many guitarists take Jazz Guitar Foundations as a complete experience in itself. For those who want to keep going, it's also a natural step toward joining one of North Star's small-group ensembles.

Why this course

What you'll walk away with.

Jazz guitar covers a lot of ground — rhythm, tone, fretboard, harmony, comping, melody, soloing, listening. Foundations works through all of it in a small group, with exercises that meet you where you are.

Over six sessions, you'll build:

  • A stronger sense of time feel, rhythm, and groove
  • Practical comping tools — voicings, accompaniment styles, playing with feel
  • Fretboard fluency and a real handle on jazz harmony
  • A growing improvisational vocabulary — phrasing, motif, narrative
  • Sharper listening and interaction on the bandstand

Your Teacher

Chris Graham

Guitar · Jazz Guitar Foundations

A native of the Twin Cities, Chris Graham first entered the local jazz scene as a young standout while still in high school, learning directly from many of the community's legends and elders. His early passion and dedication led him to New York City, where he was accepted into the prestigious New School to continue formal studies in jazz performance. Immersed in the vibrant NYC jazz world, he had the privilege of studying and performing with master musicians such as Reggie Workman, Chico Hamilton, Vic Juris, Lage Lund, Ben Monder, Tyshawn Sorey, and many others.

After several years in New York, Chris returned home to the Twin Cities and shifted his focus for a time toward steel-string acoustic guitar. During this period, he joined forces with local singer/songwriter Lucy Michelle and helped form The Velvet Lapelles, a group that enjoyed a successful run throughout the early 2010s. Around 2017, he re-entered the jazz scene and has since collaborated with many of the region's finest musicians, including Javier Santiago, Aaron Hedenstrom, Ted Olsen, Miguel Hurtado, Dan Carpel, Pete James Johnson, and more.

Hear him play

Is this class for you?

A few things to know before signing up.

Jazz Guitar Foundations is built for intermediate players. You're a good fit if:

  • You're comfortable with basic chord shapes and scales, and can play through simple chord progressions
  • You've worked through at least a few jazz tunes — or are ready to start
  • You want to go deeper on technique, harmony, comping, and improvisation

No specific theory background required — just a willingness to dig in and grow. If you're not sure whether this is the right fit, email us or book a quick call.
